newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline profits dampened by strong pound.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline profits dampened by strong pound.

text.p: Drugs group SmithKline Beecham on Tuesday reported an eight percent increase in first quarter profit despite a "dramatic" impact from the strong pound.
The currency would depress full 1997 profit by about six percent if the pound stayed at current levels, SmithKline said.
SmithKline's first-quarter pre-tax profit rose eight percent to 418 million pounds ($682.4 million) to 387 million, coming in just below analysts' expectations.
Profits would have risen 19 percent if exchange rates would had remained unchanged, the drugs firm said.
It added that revenues at its Diversified Pharmaceutical Services division had fallen 64 percent to 41 million pounds due to a change in the way it sells its services.
On a positive note, SmithKline said new products sales rose 40 percent to 354 million pounds.
